Lessons.Title: Representations of Fractions (Part 1)
ExplanationParagraphs: Original IM Grade4 Unit2 Lesson1 2021, 3-page Student Task Statements visually checked, including original source fraction-bar diagrams. Prior grade3 fractions and the meaning of 1/n are reviewed, rather than introducing unrelated measurement scales.
Warm-up What Do You Know About 1/2 (10 min): discuss a whole divided equally into two parts, shaded half and a number-line midpoint, with a partner.

Activity1 Fraction Strips (20 min): four equal-length physical paper strips each represent one whole. Keep one labelled1. Fold other strips into 2,4,8 EQUAL parts and label each1/2,1/4,1/8. Record AT LEAST TWO observations comparing the number and size of parts; teacher verifies actual folding and labels.

Activity2 Fractions, Represented (15 min): 2021 student p3 Q1 shows shade one part of two, three and five equal partitions, giving a=1/2, b=1/3, c=1/5. Q2 draw 4 new unit fraction bars for 1/6,1/8,1/10,1/12. Q3 compare 1/20 against 1/10 on the SAME whole, and explain why1/20 is smaller. Partner/teacher reviews diagrams.

Lesson synthesis (10 min): denominator specifies the count of equal parts, numerator1 selects one part. Doubling equal parts halves the unit size. Any naturally arising equivalence is contextual but not the main source learning goal.

First-party Edulytics original five-minute Cool-down, NOT source-authenticated publisher item: draw 1/6 and explain whether1/8 or1/12 is larger for two equal wholes. Teacher checks diagram and reasoning; existing digital fraction-bar interpretation Practice checks a numeric subskill only.

KeyConcepts.Title: Unit fraction
KeyConcepts.Definition: One of n equal parts of a whole.
KeyConcepts.Rule: 1/n means numerator1 selected piece among denominator n equal pieces.

KeyConcepts.Title: Same whole
KeyConcepts.Definition: Fractions are compared with identical unit wholes.
KeyConcepts.Rule: For positive denominators, more equal divisions means a smaller one-part piece.

KeyConcepts.Title: Halving strips
KeyConcepts.Definition: Fold one whole into successive equal pieces.
KeyConcepts.Example: 1/8 is half the size of1/4 on same whole.

WorkedExamples.Title: Original shaded bars
WorkedExamples.Question: Read one shaded equal part from2,3 and5 equal parts.

WorkedExamples.Title: Sixths and twelfths
WorkedExamples.Question: How do you show 1/12 using a sixths bar?
WorkedExamples.Method: Divide each sixth into2 equal parts.
WorkedExamples.Check: One twelfth is half of one sixth.

WorkedExamples.Title: Compare unit fractions
WorkedExamples.Question: Is1/20 smaller or larger than1/10 for equal wholes?
WorkedExamples.Method: Compare size of individual equal pieces.
Steps: Divide one equal whole into10 pieces.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Comparing different wholes does not demonstrate fraction size relations.
CommonMistakes.Correction: All source strips must start same length.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Choosing one piece from unequal partition sizes.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: A unit fraction requires equal-size parts.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use equal division of the whole.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming larger denominator means larger part.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Same whole split more ways makes each piece smaller.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Compare1/20 with1/10 drawn to same scale.

SummaryPoints: Original source warm-up on1/2 and four physical strips (whole, halves, fourths, eighths) with2 observations.
Original page3 shaded bars a1/2,b1/3,c1/5 and four constructed bars1/6,1/8,1/10,1/12.
1/20 is smaller than1/10 for the same whole, from equal partition sizes.
Physical strips, drawing and explanation are teacher-reviewed; numeric Practice is supplementary only.
